title: Comparable, Comparator and Sorting
summary: Natural ordering with Comparable, external orderings with Comparator, building comparators with comparing, thenComparing, reversed and nullsFirst, sorting lists and arrays, stability, sorted collections with custom orderings, the compareTo contract, and common mistakes like subtracting to compare.

cards.q: When do you use a `Comparator` instead of `Comparable`?
cards.a:
When you need an order other than the class's natural order, or the class has none you can add

`Comparable` gives one natural order, written inside the class. A `Comparator` is kept outside, so a class can be sorted many ways, including classes you cannot change.

cards.q: Why is `return a.score - b.score;` a risky `compareTo`?
cards.a:
The subtraction can overflow for large values and give the wrong sign

Any negative, zero or positive result is allowed, but `Integer.MIN_VALUE - 1` overflows to a large positive number. `Integer.compare` cannot overflow.

cards.q: A list of people is sorted by name, then sorted again by age (a stable sort). How are people of the same age ordered?
cards.a:
By name

A stable sort keeps the earlier (name) order among items that compare equal on age.
